We have a competitor that's applied to register the mark NEXORA in classes 9 and 42 — covering medical diagnostic devices and software-related services — and they've already begun marketing under that mark. Our company holds an earlier NEXORA registration in those same classes. The business team wants us to protect our commercial position without unnecessary disruption. Before I approve any enforcement strategy or filing package, I need each of you to report your findings per our standard pre-filing conference: trademark, investigations, brand, and conflicts reviewers. Let's walk through this methodically. Who'd like to start?

There's an executed 2019 coexistence letter that permits the competitor's class 42 software use — but it explicitly allows us to challenge the competitor's class 9 medical-device use.
